t: The book of original entry in which transactions are first recorded in chronological order is the:
e: Transactions are first journalised and then posted to ledger accounts; the trial balance is extracted from ledger balances to check arithmetical accuracy.

t: Which of the following is a capital receipt for a life insurance company?
o: Proceeds of a fresh issue of equity shares
Rent received on surplus office space
e: Share capital raised is a capital receipt credited to the balance sheet, whereas premium, interest and rent are revenue receipts recorded in the Revenue or Profit and Loss Account.

t: Heavy expenditure of ₹30 crore on a brand launch campaign whose benefit is expected to extend over three years is best classified as:
o: Capital expenditure, shown as a fixed asset
Revenue expenditure of the current year only
Deferred revenue expenditure, to be written off over the period of benefit
e: Revenue in nature but with benefits spread over more than one year, such expenditure is traditionally deferred and written off over the benefit period (subject to applicable standards).

t: A firm starts with capital of ₹20 lakh. It purchases furniture for ₹5 lakh in cash and takes a loan of ₹8 lakh from a bank. After these transactions, total assets are:
e: Buying furniture merely converts cash into another asset (assets stay ₹20 lakh); the loan adds ₹8 lakh of cash and liabilities, so assets = 20 + 8 = ₹28 lakh = liabilities 8 + capital 20.

t: Premium received in the second and subsequent policy years is classified in Schedule 1 of a life insurer as:
e: Schedule 1 separates first year, renewal and single premium because they have different commission rates, expense allowances and persistency implications.

t: Which of the following best describes the treatment of a renewal premium that has become due but remains unpaid within the grace period at the balance sheet date?
o: It is recognised as income with a corresponding outstanding premium receivable, as the policy is still in force
It is ignored until actually received
It is treated as a loan to the policyholder
It is credited directly to the life fund
e: Because premium is income when due and the policy remains in force during the grace period, the due premium is accrued and shown as outstanding premium under current assets.

t: Before the GST exemption of September 2025, a pure term insurance premium of ₹20,000 attracted GST at 18%. What total amount did the policyholder pay, and how much of it was premium income for the insurer?
e: GST = 18% × 20,000 = ₹3,600, so the policyholder paid ₹23,600 but only ₹20,000 is premium income; the ₹3,600 is a statutory liability remitted to government.

t: Survival benefit instalments under a money back policy are accounted by the life insurer:
o: When the agent intimates the insurer
At the end of the policy term
On the due date of the instalment
e: Like maturity claims, survival benefits are known in advance and are accounted when due, regardless of when the policyholder actually encashes them.

t: Annuity payments under an immediate annuity contract are recognised in the books of the insurer:
o: When due, as per the payment frequency of the contract
Only when the annuitant submits an existence certificate
At the end of the year in one lump sum
When the purchase price is received
e: Annuities are periodic benefits accounted when they fall due; the existence certificate is a control for payment release, not the basis of accounting.

t: A yearly-mode premium on a life policy falls due on 10 June. Up to which date can the premium be paid within the grace period?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The grace period is 30 days for yearly, half-yearly and quarterly modes (15 days for monthly mode), so the premium due on 10 June may be paid up to 10 July without the policy lapsing.

t: Claims that have been intimated and admitted but not yet paid at the balance sheet date are shown by a life insurer as:
e: Outstanding claims are a liability of the insurer and are disclosed under current liabilities in Schedule 13 until settled.

t: A 20-year endowment policy with sum assured ₹6,00,000 is made paid-up after 8 annual premiums have been paid. Ignoring bonuses, the reduced paid-up sum assured is:
e: Paid-up sum assured = Sum assured × (premiums paid / premiums payable) = 6,00,000 × 8/20 = ₹2,40,000, plus any vested bonuses.

t: Which of the following is classified as a direct expense of a life insurer's new business segment?
o: Depreciation on the corporate office building
e: Medical fees are incurred specifically for acquiring new business and can be attributed directly; audit fees, head office depreciation and directors' fees are indirect expenses needing apportionment.

t: The allowable limit on expenses of management under the IRDAI regulations is expressed primarily as:
o: A fixed rupee amount per insurer
A percentage of the different categories of premium (first year, renewal, single) across segments
e: The allowance is premium-based, with different percentages for first year regular premium (varying by policy term), renewal premium and single premium across segments such as participating, non-participating, linked and group.

t: A life insurer has gross written premium of ₹8,000 crore, operating expenses of ₹960 crore and commission of ₹400 crore. Its expenses of management ratio (operating expenses plus commission to premium) is:
e: Expenses of management ratio = (960 + 400) / 8,000 = 1,360 / 8,000 = 17%.

t: Which section of the Insurance Act, 1938 governs the manner in which the controlled fund of a life insurer is to be invested?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 27A (read with Section 27) prescribes how the assets of a life insurer are to be invested and empowers IRDAI to specify the pattern. Section 64V deals with valuation of assets and liabilities.

t: Under the IRDAI investment regulations, for a corporate debt instrument to qualify as an approved investment it should generally carry a credit rating of at least:
e: Debt instruments rated AA or above (or equivalent) qualify as approved investments; lower-rated but investment-grade paper falls under other investments subject to the applicable cap.

t: Which statement about the Fair Value Change Account of a life insurer is correct?
o: Its balance can be distributed as dividend to shareholders
It records realised profits on sale of investments
It holds unrealised gains or losses on investments carried at fair value and is not available for distribution
It is a component of current liabilities
e: The Fair Value Change Account reflects unrealised appreciation or depreciation; only realised gains or losses on sale pass through the Revenue or Profit and Loss Account.

t: A life insurer's investment policy is required to be approved by:
o: The Board of Directors, on the recommendation of the Investment Committee
e: The regulations require a board-approved investment policy reviewed at least annually, covering prudential norms, asset-liability matching and risk management, with the Investment Committee overseeing implementation.

t: A life insurer's unit linked fund has assets of ₹8,000 crore. What is the maximum it may hold in other investments (not qualifying as approved)?
e: Other investments in a linked fund are capped at 25%: 0.25 × 8,000 = ₹2,000 crore, with at least ₹6,000 crore in approved investments.

t: Which of the following is correct regarding investments backing linked liabilities?
o: They are valued at fair value with changes reflected in the fund value and the Revenue Account
They must be invested entirely in government securities
Unrealised gains are transferred to the Fair Value Change Account
e: Unit linked assets are marked to market and the gains or losses flow through the fund, since the policyholder bears the investment risk; the Fair Value Change Account treatment applies to non-linked funds.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: The statement called Receipts and Payments Account in a life insurer's annual accounts is:
o: The cash flow statement prepared under the direct method
e: IRDAI terms the cash flow statement the Receipts and Payments Account, prepared on the direct method as prescribed, showing cash flows from operating, investing and financing activities.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: As per IRDAI guidelines on appointment of statutory auditors, an audit firm may act as statutory auditor of at most how many insurance companies at a time?
e: The guidelines cap an audit firm's engagements at three insurers concurrently, in order to avoid concentration and maintain auditor independence; insurers also appoint joint auditors.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: A life insurer has share capital ₹1,500 crore, reserves and surplus ₹900 crore, a debit balance in the Profit and Loss Account of ₹200 crore and miscellaneous expenditure not written off of ₹50 crore. Its net worth is:
e: Net worth = Share capital + Reserves minus accumulated losses minus miscellaneous expenditure = 1,500 + 900 minus 200 minus 50 = ₹2,150 crore.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: ₹1,00,000 is invested at 8% per annum compounded annually. What will it amount to at the end of two years?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Future value = 1,00,000 × (1.08)^2 = 1,00,000 × 1.1664 = ₹1,16,640. Simple interest would give only ₹1,16,000.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Which statement about the Management Report that accompanies a life insurer's financial statements is correct?
o: It is prepared by the statutory auditor
It contains confirmations by management on matters such as validity of registration, solvency margin, investment pattern and overall risk exposure
It replaces the directors' report under the Companies Act
It is submitted only to the Life Insurance Council
e: The IRDAI regulations require a Management Report with specified confirmations and disclosures, signed by the management, as part of the annual financial statements.

topic: Final Accounts: Revenue Account and Balance Sheet
t: Loans given by a life insurer against policies, as well as other secured and unsecured loans, are disclosed in:
e: Schedule 9 covers loans classified by security, borrower, performance and maturity; Schedule 10 is fixed assets, 11 cash and bank balances and 12 advances and other assets.

t: A budget committee in a large organisation typically:
o: Coordinates the preparation, review and approval of functional budgets and resolves conflicts between departments
Fixes the premium rates of products
e: The budget committee, headed by a senior executive with the budget officer as secretary, coordinates the budgeting process and reviews performance reports.

t: Performance budgeting differs from traditional line-item budgeting in that it:
o: Focuses on inputs such as salaries and rent only
Links the allocation of funds to measurable outputs and objectives of programmes
Is prepared only for government departments
Ignores the previous year's figures altogether
e: Performance budgeting emphasises results and efficiency by relating expenditure to activities and outputs, rather than merely listing expense heads.

t: A capital expenditure budget of a life insurer would include:
o: Planned purchase of new data-centre hardware and office premises
Death claims expected during the year
e: The capital budget plans long-term asset acquisitions; commission, claims and premium belong to revenue budgets.

t: Economic Value Added (EVA) of a business is computed as:
o: Net profit after tax minus a charge for the capital employed at the cost of capital
Sales minus cost of goods sold
Market value of equity minus book value of equity
e: EVA = NOPAT minus (Capital employed × Cost of capital); a positive EVA shows that the business earns more than the cost of the capital it uses.

t: Integrated Reporting, as promoted by the International Integrated Reporting Council, aims to:
o: Consolidate the accounts of all group companies
Explain how an organisation creates value over time using financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and natural capitals
e: Integrated Reporting connects strategy, governance, performance and prospects across six capitals in a single concise report for providers of financial capital.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: A life insurer takes office premises on a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards of ownership. Under AS 19 this is classified as:
e: AS 19 classifies a lease as a finance lease when substantially all risks and rewards incidental to ownership are transferred; the asset and liability are then recognised by the lessee.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: A listed life insurance company must disclose basic and diluted earnings per share in accordance with:
e: AS 20 (Earnings per Share) requires EPS disclosure, calculated using profit attributable to equity shareholders and the weighted average number of shares.

topic: Accounting Standard (Applicable to Life Insurance Companies)
t: When the carrying amount of an asset exceeds its recoverable amount, the insurer is required to recognise an impairment loss under:
e: AS 28 (Impairment of Assets) requires the carrying amount to be written down to the recoverable amount (higher of net selling price and value in use).

t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits:
o: Payment of any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to buy insurance
Issue of a policy without a medical examination
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 41 bars rebating; contravention attracts a penalty of up to ₹10 lakh.

t: IRDAI requires every insurer to maintain a solvency ratio of at least:
e: The control level of solvency is 150% (ASM at least 1.5 times RSM); falling below it triggers regulatory action including a financial plan for restoring solvency.

t: A life insurer reports value of new business of ₹400 crore on annualised premium equivalent of ₹1,600 crore. Its VNB margin is:
e: VNB margin = VNB / APE = 400 / 1,600 = 25%, meaning each ₹100 of annualised new business premium is expected to generate ₹25 of present value of future profits.

t: Annualised premium equivalent (APE) is computed as:
o: Regular premium plus 10% of single premium
Regular premium plus 100% of single premium
10% of regular premium plus single premium
e: APE = 100% of annualised regular (first year) premium + 10% of single premium, which places single-premium sales on a comparable footing with regular-premium sales.

t: Which of the following statements about financial ratio analysis is incorrect?
o: Ratios are most useful when compared over time or against peers
Ratios can be distorted by differences in accounting policies between companies
A single ratio in isolation gives a complete picture of financial health
Ratios help convert absolute figures into comparable relationships
e: No single ratio is sufficient; ratios must be read together, over time and against benchmarks, and interpreted in the light of accounting policies and business context.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was constituted as a statutory body in:
e: Although the IRDA Act was passed in December 1999, the Authority was constituted in April 2000 and the first private life insurers were licensed later that year.

t: Bima Sugam, promoted by IRDAI, is intended to be:
o: A new public sector life insurer
A digital marketplace for buying, selling and servicing insurance policies and settling claims
A reinsurance pool for crop insurance
The new name for the Insurance Ombudsman
e: Bima Sugam is envisaged as a one-stop online insurance platform under IRDAI's Insurance for All by 2047 vision, alongside Bima Vistaar and Bima Vahak.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: Opportunity cost in financial decision-making refers to:
o: The cash outlay of a project
The benefit forgone from the next best alternative use of a resource
The depreciation charged on an asset
e: Opportunity cost is the return given up by choosing one option over the best alternative; it is relevant for decisions even though it is not recorded in the books.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: An investment of ₹2 crore generated annual net profit of ₹30 lakh. Its return on investment is:
e: ROI = 30 lakh / 2 crore = 30 / 200 = 15%.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

topic: Application of Financial Management Concepts in the Insurance Industry
t: Immunisation of a bond portfolio against interest rate risk is achieved when:
o: The duration of assets equals the duration of liabilities
The portfolio is invested in equities
e: When asset and liability durations are matched, a small change in interest rates affects both values equally, protecting the surplus; this is a core ALM technique.

t: Following the GST Council's decision of September 2025, with effect from 22 September 2025 individual life insurance policies (term, endowment, ULIP) are:
e: The 56th GST Council meeting exempted all individual life and health insurance policies (and their reinsurance) from GST with effect from 22 September 2025; earlier term plans attracted 18%.

t: Income of an approved pension fund set up by an insurer under Section 10(23AAB) of the Income-tax Act is:
e: Section 10(23AAB) exempts the income of a fund set up by LIC or any other insurer under a pension scheme approved by IRDAI, to encourage retirement savings.

topic: Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Act
t: Following the 2023 amendment to the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, the ownership threshold for identifying the beneficial owner of a company client is:
e: The threshold was reduced from 25% to 10% of shares, capital or profits, widening the net of individuals to be identified as beneficial owners during customer due diligence.

topic: Anti-Money Laundering Guidelines and Prevention of Money Laundering (PML) Act
t: The Cash Transaction Report for a calendar month must be furnished to FIU-IND by:
o: The last day of the same month
Within 7 working days of each transaction
e: CTRs are filed monthly by the 15th day of the succeeding month, whereas STRs are filed within seven working days of determination of suspicion.
